Subject: Service Guarantee Matrix & Measurement SOW (MosaicCloud appendix)

Hi Chris / Elena —

Please find our proposed appendix below. We've kept it concise so you can paste into your template; attached are a spreadsheet matrix (service-guarantee-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a small sample telemetry extract (redwood-observability-sample.log) to illustrate the evidence format. If this looks good we can convert to your procurement template and circulate a DocuSign SOW reference.

--- BEGIN APPENDIX ---
1) Scope and Applicability
- Applies to Redwood-hosted inference endpoints provisioned for MosaicCloud under deal MOSAIC-2026-055.
- Metrics are computed per routing policy (region / model variant) and aggregated for account-level crediting.

2) Metric Definitions
- Availability: percentage of requests returning a 2xx response within the request timeout (default 120s). Formula: Availability = (successful requests) / (total requests) * 100. Successful excludes client-side network failures; Redwood provides evidence of inbound request receipt for those cases.
- Latency (Interactive - streaming): token-level p99 tail latency measured on server ingress-to-first-byte for each generated token and session-level end-to-end latency (session completion p95).
- Latency (Batch - non-streaming): request-level p95/p99 measured on server-side request completion.

3) Measurement Sources and Reconciliation
- Primary sources: server-side telemetry (internal tracing + API request logs) retained for 90 days; global synthetic probes (every region, 1-minute cadence) retained for 180 days.
- Reconciliation: For any window where synthetic and telemetry differ by >5 percentage points on availability or >10% on latency, Redwood will perform a reconciliation procedure and provide both raw logs and probe outputs.

4) Clock Sync and Attribution
- Redwood maintains NTP/chrony across all serving clusters with max drift tolerated = 500ms for crediting purposes. Customer-supplied probe timestamps will be aligned in reconciliation using jump-correction metadata.

5) Sampling and Minimums
- Minimum traffic threshold to trigger credit: 1,000 requests for the affected routing policy during the measurement day. If below threshold, the window is not eligible for credit but is included in root cause analysis.

6) Multi-region Aggregation
- Per-region availability is computed independently. Account-level availability = weighted average by successful request count across regions. Credits are computed on the account-level shortfall but Redwood will provide a breakdown by region in the evidence package.

7) Service Credit Calculation (example)
- SLO: Monthly account-level availability target = 99.95%
- Observation: In September the account-level availability = 99.70%
- Shortfall = 0.25% = (99.95 - 99.70)
- Credit formula (monthly): Credit = min( (Shortfall / 1.0%) * Monthly recurring fees, Monthly cap )
  Example: Shortfall 0.25% => (0.25 / 1.0) = 0.25x monthly fees => credit = 25% of monthly recurring platform fee, subject to a cap of 50% of monthly fees. Credits are applied as bill credits in the following billing cycle.

8) Escalation and Audit Evidence
- Evidence package for any credit event includes: API request logs (timestamp, request-id, status, latency), synthetic probe logs with timestamps and payloads, ingress traces for affected time windows, and a reconciliation memo describing variance and root cause.
- Redwood permits a one-time customer audit of telemetry for the affected window; audit requests must be made within 60 days of the event.

9) Exceptions and Maintenance
- Planned maintenance windows announced >= 72 hours in advance and listed in the Redwood Console are excluded from credit calculations during the maintenance window.
- Emergency mitigations and force majeure are handled per standard SOW clauses; Redwood will provide post-incident evidence and remediation timelines.

10) Reporting and Monitoring
- Redwood will provide a monthly SLA report (CSV) with per-route availability and latency percentiles and a weekly synthetic-probe health summary.

11) Mutual Action Plan / Next Steps
- Redwood to produce a formatted appendix in MosaicCloud template and return via DocuSign reference by Fri 01-Oct EOD. (If you prefer an earlier turnaround we can prioritize.)
- Redwood to ingest MosaicCloud's list of protected routes and provide a per-route SLO mapping within five business days after SOW acceptance.

--- END APPENDIX ---

Attachment: service-guarantee-matrix-v1.xlsx (sheet contains columns: Metric | Definition | Measurement Source | Cadence | Attribution Window | Threshold | Credit Formula Example)

Evidence sample included in redwood-observability-sample.log shows our standard log columns (timestamp, region, request_id, route, model, status, latency_ms).

If you'd like we can also provide a short worked example for a multi-region burst outage showing the per-region decomposition and the account-level credit math.
